S5.01.note: The header shows the app name, model, provider, git branch and folder. It does not show the conversation title, and it has no action buttons; actions are typed commands.
steps: Open Terminal, type agi and press Enter.
Wait for the start screen to appear.
Look at the top two rows: the app name, version, model and provider, then the second row with the counts and the context meter.
Type a short message, press Enter and scroll the chat.
Check the top rows are still on screen. Compare with Expected (a persistent header that shows where you are).
S5.01.where: Run agi in a terminal, then look at the top two rows of the screen

S5.07.note: The terminal app has no navigation sidebar and no search box in the shell. Closest found: /history search <text> filters the Sessions list to entries containing the text (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs). Searched apps/cli/src for sidebar, search and recent wording.

S5.08.note: This is a typed slash command only; there is no button for it.
steps: Start agi and send one message so the chat has text.
Type /new and press Enter.
Look for the line Started new conversation. and a cleared chat. Compare with Expected (a fresh conversation).
S5.08.where: /new (type it at the prompt and press Enter)

S5.10.needs: an earlier saved conversation in the same folder
S5.10.note: The Recent activity rows on the start screen are plain text and do not open when selected; opening is done from the /resume Sessions list.
steps: Send a message in a folder, quit agi, then run agi again in the same folder.
Look at the start screen for Recent activity, with rows such as 2h ago and a title.
Type /resume and press Enter to open the Sessions list.
Press Enter on a row and check that the chosen conversation opens.
S5.10.where: /resume (type it at the prompt and press Enter)

S5.12.needs: saved conversations from several days; a date heading only appears for chats older than a week
S5.12.note: Date grouping appears only in the shell listing, not in the in-app Sessions list (/resume), which is flat. The code says This Week and uses a date instead of Older.
steps: Quit agi, then in Terminal run: agi session list
Look for group headings Today, Yesterday, This Week, or a calendar date.
Compare with Expected (Today, Yesterday, This week, Older).
S5.12.where: agi session list (run in Terminal, outside agi)

labels.text: ↑↓ navigate   Enter resume   r rename   Esc close

S5.13.needs: at least one saved conversation in this folder
S5.13.note: The row marks the cursor position, not the open conversation; no active-row marker was found in the code.
steps: Type /resume and press Enter.
Look at each row: a short id, date and time, message count and title.
Move with Up or Down. The arrow mark marks the cursor row.
Press Enter on a row and check that the chosen conversation opens.
S5.13.where: /resume (type it at the prompt and press Enter)

S5.14.note: The terminal app shows no project rows. Only shell commands were found: agi projects list (prints No projects in your AGI account. when empty, apps/cli/src/lib.rs) and agi -C <folder> to start a session in a folder. No project actions were found.

S5.15.needs: a running or finished background task
S5.15.note: Tasks are text in the /tasks list, not rows in a sidebar, and they are not selected with the keyboard.
steps: Start background work, such as a sub-agent or background terminal task, in a conversation (how the task starts was not traced).
Type /tasks and press Enter.
Look for the task list with each task and its state. Compare with Expected (tasks shown apart from chats, with state).
Type /tasks show <id> using an id from the list and check that the task output opens.
S5.15.where: /tasks (type it at the prompt and press Enter)

S5.17.note: The running marker is text and a spinner only. No separate screen-reader marker was found in the code, and there is no navigation list to mark.
steps: Start agi and send a prompt that takes a few seconds, such as a question that needs a tool.
Look at the spinner line above the input, such as 3s, which shows still working after about 10 seconds with no text.
Look at the header second row for the working count.
When two or more tools run at once, look for the line with working at once (subagents for sub-agents). Compare with Expected (running work is marked).
S5.17.where: Send a prompt in agi, then look at the spinner line above the input and the header second row

S5.18.needs: a permission mode that asks before tools run
S5.18.note: The marker is text in the status line and header, not a mark on a list row, because the terminal app has no list of items to mark.
steps: Start agi and press Shift+Tab until the mode label in the status bar shows a mode that asks before running tools.
Send a prompt that needs a tool, such as reading or writing a file.
Look at the spinner line for Waiting for your approval and at the header second row for the awaiting input count.
Answer the approval prompt that opens. Compare with Expected (an item blocked on the user is marked).
S5.18.where: Shift+Tab to a permission mode that asks before tools, then send a prompt that uses a tool

S5.20.note: No overflow menu was found. The /resume Sessions list has only Enter (resume) and r (rename). No /pin, /archive, /move, /delete or /share command was found in apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs, apps/cli/src/command_registry.rs or apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs. /rename and /fork exist as typed commands.

S5.21.needs: a saved conversation in this folder
S5.21.note: Rename does not happen inside the row. The r key fills the prompt with /rename <id>, and Enter runs it. Escape to cancel was not verified for that prompt.
steps: Type /resume and press Enter.
Use Up or Down to pick a row.
Press r. The prompt line fills with /rename and the conversation id.
Type the new name and press Enter.
Reopen /resume and check the row shows the new title. Compare with Expected (renamed in place, the title persists).
S5.21.where: /resume, then press r on a row (Sessions list)

labels.text: Type to filter   ↑↓ navigate   Enter select   Esc cancel

S5.26.note: The palette lists slash commands only; app destinations such as chats or folders were not found in it. The default key shown is /; ctrl+p applies only when set in config.
steps: Start agi and make sure the prompt line is empty.
Press / to open the Commands list.
Type a word such as model to filter, use Up and Down, then press Enter on a command.
Check that the list filters and the chosen command runs. Compare with Expected (searches and runs app commands).
S5.26.where: / (press / on an empty prompt line to open the Commands list)

S5.27.note: Both views print into the chat as text; no dedicated overlay was found for them.
steps: Type /keybindings and press Enter.
Look for the Keybindings list with entries such as Open command palette and Cycle permission mode.
Type /help and press Enter, then look for the Keyboard shortcuts: section.

S5.29.note: No profile menu was found. /status prints Account: signed in, <tier> plan, or not signed in (agi login) (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs). Sign-out is the typed /logout. No settings or plan menu was found.

S5.30.note: Only commands and shortcuts are in /help. No help centre link or support contact was found; feedback is /feedback or /bug.
steps: Type /help and press Enter.
Look at the command list and the Keyboard shortcuts: section.
Type /feedback with no words to see its usage text. Compare with Expected (help centre, support contact, feedback and shortcuts in one place).

S5.31.needs: a browser on this computer; eligibility was not checked in the code
S5.31.note: No visible Upgrade entry is drawn on the terminal screen. /upgrade, /pricing and /extra-usage open the plans web page in the browser.
steps: Type /upgrade and press Enter.
Look for Opened plans and upgrades in your browser: with the link, or Plans and upgrades: with the link if the browser did not open.
Compare with Expected (takes an eligible user into the plan upgrade flow).
S5.31.where: /upgrade (type it at the prompt and press Enter)

labels.text: AGI Cloud: unreachable. Check your connection, then run /status to try again.

S5.32.needs: a Managed Cloud session and a way to turn the network off
S5.32.note: No persistent indicator and no reconnect button were found; reconnecting means running /status again. In Local mode the line says AGI Cloud is not used by this session.
steps: Start agi in a Managed Cloud session, not Local.
Type /status and press Enter, then look for AGI Cloud: reachable with a time in ms.
Turn off the network, type /status again and look for the unreachable line.
Turn the network back on and run /status again to reconnect.

S5.34.needs: an older build than the published one, an internet connection, and a privacy mode other than Local
S5.34.note: This is a one-time notice, not a persistent indicator. The check is skipped when AGIWORKFORCE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK is set or updates.check_on_startup is off. The start screen also shows a what's-new line for a just-installed build when a release summary exists.
steps: Run agi update --check in Terminal and wait for the verdict.
Look for An update is available. Install it with: agi update --install, or the up-to-date line.
Start agi and watch the top of the chat for an agi version is available notice with the same install command.
Compare with Expected (the app says a new release is available and how to get it).
S5.34.where: agi update --check (run in Terminal, outside agi); the startup notice appears on its own when a newer release is found
